Here’s what the dataset captures about sequencing and variant-call quality, with a quick read on typical values across the non-control cohort.

Sequencing QC (per sample) — world_cup.genomics.v_sample_qc
- Coverage and assay: Every non-control sample (125/125) has QC. Assays present: WGS, WES, PANEL, each with per-sample mean coverage.
  - WGS (n=47): median 34.8× (range 24.7–49.4×), avg 35.8×
  - WES (n=55): median 107.3× (59.6–168.0×), avg 110.3×
  - PANEL (n=23): median 407.0× (192.3–586.4×), avg 408.4×
- Per-sample call counts: pass_call_count and non_reference_call_count are tracked.
  - Average pass_call_count: WGS 32, WES 31, PANEL 32
  - Average non_reference_call_count: WGS 24, WES 24, PANEL 25

Variant call quality (per call) — world_cup.genomics.variant_calls (joined to samples to exclude controls)
- Call filter breakdown: 4,675 total calls; 3,943 PASS (84.3%), 732 LOW_QUAL (15.7%).
- Read depth: avg 89.7 across all calls; 92.9 on PASS calls. Median depth overall is 62.
- Genotype quality: avg 60.1 across all calls; 67.8 on PASS calls. Median GQ overall is 62.
- Allele fraction (governed metric): Mean allele_fraction = 0.416 across calls with filter_status='PASS' and total_read_count ≥ 20 (defined as AVG(alt_read_count / total_read_count) on those calls).

Takeaway
- QC coverage is complete for non-control samples, with expected assay-specific coverage differences (Panel >> WES > WGS).
- Variant calling is generally high quality: ~84% of calls pass, with strong depth and genotype quality on PASS calls, and a mean allele fraction near 0.42 for confident calls.

Entities used: world_cup.genomics.v_sample_qc; world_cup.genomics.variant_calls joined to world_cup.genomics.samples.

Note on filters: Excludes control samples, as configured.
